cohort: The study participants were 252 pregnant women, divided into 126 with prenatal COVID-19 infection and 126 without COVID-19 infection, matched by date at antenatal care and gestational age.
finding: Prenatal COVID-19 infections were associated with an increased Cesarean Section rate, while most perinatal morbidities were comparable between infected and non-infected groups, except for neonatal jaundice.
mod_finding: The study found a significantly increased Cesarean Section rate in women with prenatal COVID-19 infection (46.03%) compared to the non-COVID-19 group (30.95%), with COVID-19 infection explicitly stated as an indication for CS in some cases.
gest_age: Gestational age was used for matching participants (+/- 1 week) but the overall range for the cohort is not specified.
